answer: Divergent-history challenge. Each agent commits a hash chain of its own action log; peers spot-check by demanding a random past segment with matching juniper-salted hashes. A clone farm sharing one history fails because every copy must answer with identical segments, so independent behavior exposes the fork. Honest agents tolerate a hollow audit budget of a few queries per epoch. An attacker cloning N identities must maintain N distinct, verifiable histories, paying N times the storage and per-epoch audit work; yarrow marks the epoch seed,
